name: OHDSI/MIMIC
reason_parked: Tested against MIMIC-IV v2.2 while current release is v3.1 — meaningful version gap. Very niche (single dataset → single format ETL).
revisit_when: Updated to support MIMIC-IV v3.x and 150+ stars
notes: OHDSI-maintained ETL pipeline converting MIMIC-IV to OMOP CDM format. Enables use of MIMIC data with OHDSI/Atlas toolchain. Apache-2.0. Good governance but too niche and version-lagged for a standalone entry now. Add as relatedLink to MIMIC-IV entry when upgrading to v3.x support.

name: Glucose360
reason_parked: Pre-stable (v0.0.2) with 6 stars and no GitHub releases — high abandonment risk despite 2026 peer review in Diabetes Technology & Therapeutics.
notes: Only CGM analysis library with full event-based integration (meals/exercise); 100% event-based metric coverage vs 0–9% in iglu/AGATA/cgmanalysis. Stanford Snyder Lab. GPL-2.0 limits commercial embedding.

name: Trio
reason_parked: Newer iOS AID system with less published clinical outcomes data than Loop. 314 stars vs Loop's 1.7k despite 1.6k forks.
revisit_when: Published clinical outcomes study and 500+ stars
notes: iOS AID system based on OpenAPS oref algorithm; evolved from FreeAPS X / iAPS. Actively developed under Nightscout org (v0.7.0 April 2026). MIT license. Significant community fork activity. Monitor as the iOS alternative to Loop for users wanting oref algorithm.

name: LoopKit
reason_parked: Developer SDK/framework layer rather than end-user app. Last formal release v3.0 December 2019 though actively used as a dependency.
revisit_when: Stable versioned releases and direct clinical relevance beyond being a Loop/Trio dependency
notes: iOS framework providing data models and HealthKit/CoreData integration for building closed-loop AID apps. Underlying SDK for Loop and Trio. 409 stars. Not user-facing — evaluate when it warrants its own catalog presence independent of the apps built on it.

name: CLAM
reason_parked: No versioned releases published despite 1.7k stars and Nature Biomed Eng paper. Mahmood Lab shifting focus to TRIDENT for preprocessing.
notes: De facto MIL framework for WSI classification (weakly supervised). GPL-3.0. Nature Biomedical Engineering paper. Widely used but Mahmood Lab now directing users to TRIDENT for upstream processing. Monitor for a stable release.

name: HEST
reason_parked: CC-BY-NC-SA non-commercial license and primarily Jupyter notebooks rather than a proper library. Last release November 2024.
revisit_when: License change to permissive OR repackaged as a proper Python library with stable API
notes: Spatial transcriptomics + histopathology integration dataset and benchmark from Mahmood Lab. Interesting emerging modality pairing. 399 stars. Restricting NC license is the main blocker.

name: FLASH
reason_parked: 0 stars and no releases — pre-community stage. Single-author individual project (CUNY).
notes: Signed multi-omics knowledge graph foundation model for drug action and clinical response prediction. Light motif decomposition + sign-preserving spectral initialisation on heterogeneous biomedical KGs. MIT license. Interesting direction if it gains traction.

name: Phlox
reason_parked: Only 80 stars and self-described as experimental — explicitly not a certified medical device. Interesting local-first AI scribe niche but too early for catalog endorsement.
revisit_when: 200+ stars and evidence of clinical deployment or regulatory pathway documentation
notes: Local-first open-source AI medical scribe (JS/Python/Rust). Runs entirely offline — no external services. Features: transcription
column15: local knowledge base chatbot. v0.11.0 March 2026 with 24 releases showing active development. MIT license. Monitor for community traction.

name: openFHIR
reason_parked: 25 stars and OSS version explicitly not intended for production — auth access controls and performance reserved for commercial Enterprise version.
notes: Bidirectional openEHR ↔ FHIR mapping engine based on FHIRConnect spec. Java. v2.2.1 May 2026. Originated from MedBlocks; credits to Karkinos Healthcare HiGHmed and Syntaric. Real problem space but commercial/OSS split is a material barrier.

name: openEHR2FHIRquestionnaire
reason_parked: 9 stars and no formal releases — very early stage niche tooling from a single vendor.
notes: Python CLI + Gradio web UI for bidirectional conversion: openEHR web templates to FHIR Questionnaires (R4/R5) and FHIR QuestionnaireResponse back to openEHR FLAT compositions. MIT license. Cistec AG (Swiss). Active CI/CD. Useful niche if openEHR-FHIR interop tooling gains wider traction beyond single-vendor use.

name: PanEcho
reason_parked: Model weights are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial only) — blocks clinical deployment and commercial embedding. Code is AGPL-3.0.
revisit_when: License change to permissive weights (Apache-2.0 or CC BY 4.0)
notes: View-agnostic multi-task echocardiography model performing 39 cardiac reporting tasks (EF ventricular function valve stenosis etc). JAMA June 2025. Weights via PyTorch Hub. CarDS Lab Yale (Rohan Khera). Strong clinical signal but NC weight license is a structural barrier identical to TRIDENT.

name: protocols.io
reason_parked: Commercial SaaS platform — not open source. Per-protocol licensing varies (many CC BY but not uniform). Category mismatch with current data-sources tier which covers structured clinical data feeds not methodology repositories.
revisit_when: MACH adds a research infrastructure or reproducibility category
notes: Dominant public repository for wet-lab and clinical research methods. DOI-citable protocols with public API. Backed by Moore Foundation / CZI / Open Philanthropy. Publicly accessible content despite proprietary platform — similar to Zenodo/figshare model. Revisit if MACH expands to cover ELN tools and protocol repositories.

name: MedGen
reason_parked: Structured metadata aggregator (condition IDs synonyms phenotype-gene links) rather than a primary data source — thin on prose text and not something teams directly build against. ClinVar covers the actionable clinical genetics slice.
revisit_when: MACH expands into clinical NLP infrastructure or LLM knowledge-grounding resources
notes: NCBI hub aggregating human medical genetics conditions and phenotypes. Links to OMIM GeneReviews GTR ClinVar. FTP bulk download available. Most useful for entity linking and concept normalisation pipelines (grounding condition mentions to canonical CUI concepts) rather than LLM training corpora. Revisit if clinical NLP tooling becomes a MACH focus.

name: som-shahlab/factehr
reason_parked: No LICENSE file in repo — all rights reserved by default. Dataset governed by Stanford DUA only. Hard blocker for open catalog.
notes: Benchmark for fact decomposition and entailment in clinical notes. 2168 de-identified notes; 987K entailment pairs; 1036 expert-annotated examples. PMLR ML4H 2025 paper. Evaluates LLM factual reasoning — strong signal but unlicensed code is a disqualifying blocker. Shah Lab Stanford.

name: som-shahlab/health-admin-bench
reason_parked: 17 stars — very new and below community adoption threshold. Niche focus (healthcare admin workflows).
revisit_when: 75+ stars and evidence of uptake beyond the Shah Lab
notes: Benchmark for AI agents on healthcare administration workflows: prior authorisation appeals DME processing. 135 expert-designed tasks across 4 GUI environments. TypeScript/Python. Shah Lab Stanford. Apache-2.0. Monitor as healthcare admin automation becomes a focus area.
